quest.title: Ode to Flower and Cloud
quest.description: When you've got some leisure time, how about taking a stroll through Mondstadt's streets and seeing if there's anything to do?
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x60, Hero's Wit x3, Mora x30000

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hiiii~! Can we help with anything?

dialogues.speaker: Sara
dialogues.text: Sorry, it's the Windblume Festival! There's nothing I can hand off to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... nothing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... let's go ask someone else then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello, is there anything here you need help with?

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: Ahahaha! That's a good one! You two, helping me during the Windblume Festival? Hahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Weird... Let's go to the Adventurers' Guild!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Katheryne! You got any commissions for us?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: My apologies. During the Windblume Festival, there are far fewer commissions available. There's nothing I can give to you at this moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh? The Adventurers' Guild too!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, wh—what do we do now? Have we been... fired?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who'd have thought...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No! Paimon's not giving up that easily! We gotta try again!

talks.objective: Talk to Flora at the flower shop

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Flora, do you have anything you need help with?

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Hee-hee — nope.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that b—because of the Windblume Festival...? Huh... what is that, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: *gasp* You two haven't heard of the Windblume Festival?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Windblume... Soooo — some kinda... windy, flower-planting kinda thing...?

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: The Windblume Festival is a Mondstadt tradition — a festival of love and freedom. It's a time of celebration and partying in the city.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: At this time of year, we offer Windblumes to the great Anemo Archon, Barbatos, as a sign of reverence and love. We also give flowers to our beloved... a very important tradition.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: My shop is bursting with customers every Windblume... I guess it's a nice problem to have! Haha.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are Windblumes?

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: The Windblume is the symbol of this festival, a flower that represents freedom and the spirit of the wind...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Soooo what does a Windblume look like?

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Haha... that's a long story...

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: My grandma said that even she hadn't been born when the Windblume first appeared. It must have been hundreds of years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: I don't know why, exactly, but everyone seems to choose dandelions when they wanna give a gift of "Windblumes."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So in other words, for the people of Mondstadt, Windblume means dandelion?

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Hehe... something like that, anyway. At least, that's what we believe in my family.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Incorrect!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Ahem... I heard everything you were saying and couldn't help but... You were talking about Windblumes, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's Quinn from the fruit stall! Wanna join us?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: No, no — I'm just here to set the record straight. Windblume doesn't mean the dandelion, but the Windwheel Aster.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Greetings to you too, Quinn!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Uh... Flora, surely there must have been plenty of customers buying Windwheel Asters from your shop recently?

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Hee-hee, uh-huh!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Haha, you see! We loyal Windwheel Aster advocates are upholding our economic duty!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: The Windwheel Aster is both a symbol of Mondstadt and an embodiment of the windmill, representing both wind and freedom. That's what makes it the one, true Windblume!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Who's with me!? Windwheel Aster! The true Windblume!

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Ehh...

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: Oh? Are you sure about that?

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Bea, you're here too!

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: Hehe, the Windblume... Isn't that the Cecilia?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Really?

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Oh? So a Windblume is a Cecilia...? That's the first I've heard of—

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Wh— ...Don't be ridiculous!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Listen. Yes, there may be some controversy over the definition of Windblume... but it is the widely held belief among the people of Mondstadt, that the Windblume is the Windwheel Aster! Not the dandelion!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: There's history to both flowers, you'd know if you asked around! And as for the Cecilia? Give me a break...

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Just dropping the facts over here, no need to look at me like that...

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: You...! Hmph — whatever, I'm not talking to you.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Huh? Bea? Bea!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Weird, what's up with her...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Did I say something wrong? Eh... Windblume is as Windblume does, what can I say...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... what?

response.speaker: Flora
response.text: Haha, stop arguing already!

response.speaker: Quinn
response.text: Maybe I should... go and apologize to her after closing... hmm...

response.speaker: Quinn
response.text: ...I don't understand why she's upset, but what I do know is that I will have to apologize regardless. *sigh* That's life, I guess.

response.speaker: Flora
response.text: Aww... Seeing them together like that really gives me that Windblume feeling.

response.speaker: Flora
response.text: Freedom, the Anemo Archon, sweethearts...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, yeah, that sounds great and all...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But none of you can even agree over what a Windblume is...

response.speaker: Flora
response.text: You're right, but isn't that typical of us Mondstadt folk?

response.speaker: Flora
response.text: *sigh* Well, between the delicious food, exquisite drink, and fresh flowers... Traveler, I hope you get to enjoy yourself during the festival, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It sounds like such a happy festival! Even if the whole Windblume thing is still a total mystery...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's look around and see what this is all about!

choices.text: I'm new here, your local customs are a bit confusing for me.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: When's it gonna be my turn... Gah! I'm getting nervous just thinking about writing a love poem...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tone-Deaf Bard, what are you up to? What's with all the people?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Aha! You're right on time. Take a look at my students. What do you think? Not bad, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Students? Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean the people anxiously scratching their heads?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Anxiously? Why, these people are deep in concentration, diligently searching for heartfelt rhetoric to convey their romantic affections.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-huh... Seems a bit suspicious to Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hehe, so, I guess you've already found out about the Windblume Festival, then?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: How are you finding Mondstadt in such a festive mood? Do you like it?

choices.text: It's certainly buzzing with excitement and happiness.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Paimon, what about you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Paimon could be persuaded with some delicious food-related bribery!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Ah, I think you'll come around then. Speaking of which, I'll bet you two don't have a lot on your plate right now.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Loafing around all day, no commissions to take or people to help...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hahaha... If you've noticed that, then congratulations — you've taken your first step toward understanding the Windblume Festival!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah? Hey — why do you sound so pleased with yourself!?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The Windblume Festival doesn't just belong to the Anemo Archon, but to all Mondstadt citizens looking for love. Anyone who wants to find love must do everything for themselves over the festive period.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: In addition, many people take this period as an opportunity to resolve other matters of the heart. It's not surprising that you two haven't been able to find any commissions, that's just the Windblume Festival tradition.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But don't you worry, you won't feel lonely while I'm around.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: On that note, I think it's about time you two got a deeper understanding of Mondstadt's culture and customs. I need a couple of assistants. What do you say?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Assistants? What kind of assistants?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Ahahaha... See these anxious-looking folks here?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: They're looking to learn the secrets of love, so they came to me to learn how to compose love poems. I accepted, of course, because I was only too happy to charge a tuition fee.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Soon, they'll come to me in turn and pour their hearts out, telling me about their romantic trials and tribulations. Then, I'll give them suggestions based on their individual circumstances.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: At least, that's what I was going to do... But having seen you two suffering with nothing to do... I think I'll let you handle it instead.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: You've traveled far and wide and seen so much, it would be a waste not to put those experiences to good use. They could use your help!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, save us the nonsense... You just want to speed up your sales. That desperate for Mora, huh?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: There are limited-edition wines for sale during the Windblume Festival... I need every last Mora to make sure I get my fill.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh... Spoken like a true drunkard...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Alright then, let's get started. I'll be joining you, of course.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I'll give you a few prompts, and you can make suggestions based on them. Hehe, not as taxing as you thought, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You really love the sound of your own voice, don't you!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Come on now, you're Mondstadt's Honorary Knight, the people trust you! It's only natural for you to have this opportunity to showcase yourself.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Now listen up, if you see me make this gesture... it means I think they should forge ahead and seize the opportunity.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But if you see me make this gesture... it means I think they should play it safe and avoid being hasty.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: And if I make this gesture... it means I think they should give up while they're ahead and avoid any emotional over-investment.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: You got that, Traveler?

choices.text: Can you repeat it once more?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Okay... make sure you pay attention this time.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: That's decided then!

choices.text: Still not exactly sure how to celebrate the festival itself.

talks.objective: Listen to and solve the troubles of the citizenry

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon heard that you were seeking help from the Bard over there? We're his assistants! Why not talk to us?

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Huh...? I—I'd barely plucked up the courage to talk to the bard, is he not available...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw... don't be shy! It doesn't matter who you talk to, at the end of the day you've still gotta talk to your prospective sweetheart, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Be brave! Let's hear it!

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: *sigh* Here goes. Th—There is someone I like...

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Marla... She's cute and hardworking — always helping her family out with the farm work. And sometimes, she gets so tired, she takes a nap on a bench by the side of the road.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is she from the city?

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: N—No, she lives in Springvale, quite a way from me. And... because of my family...

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: *sigh* Let's just say that our families are quite different. My father objects to us being together.

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: But Marla and I have found a way to work around it! Whenever we want to meet, we go stargazing at Starsnatch Cliff.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... sounds like you two are getting along just fine!

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: We are... So, what I came to discuss today doesn't so much concern Marla... as my father.

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: My father is quite conservative and very strict. Still, it's my fault that I've never told him how I really feel.

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: I—I'm thinking, if I use this opportunity to offer a Windblume to my father, and formally ask for his approval at the same time... maybe he'll support us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you planning to say?

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: I wanna tell him that, even though Marla doesn't come from a wealthy family, her kind heart and hardworking nature are things that Mora can't buy!

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: ...Does that sound too childish? I... I hope he doesn't yell at me... Uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Awwww... there-there...

choices.text: I think you should tell him. Be brave and seize the opportunity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Tell him what's in your heart. Use the love between you and Marla to move him. Shouldn't it be something to celebrate?

response.speaker: Marvin
response.text: I see... understood. Thank you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Another thing, didn't you say you were going to give flowers to your father? What about Marla? Don't you wanna give her something?

response.speaker: Marvin
response.text: Oh! Ah, now that you mention it, I wanted the bard to teach me how to compose a love poem...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes, better not neglect her.

response.speaker: Marvin
response.text: Of course, and I'll give her some flowers too... Yeah, I—I'll pick some later.

response.speaker: Marvin
response.text: Thank you for your help!

choices.text: I think you should take some more time to consider things.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, if your father is set in his ways, approaching this head-on might not be the best thing to do...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not to mention, the Windblume Festival is too formal an occasion. Why not be a bit more spontaneous about it?

choices.text: I think that's a bad idea. Best not to tell him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh, Paimon thinks so too, you don't wanna get shouted at. Don't make any rash moves!

talks.objective: Listen to and solve the troubles of the citizenry

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi! We heard you had something you wanted to discuss with the bard? We're his assistants, you can talk to us instead!

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: It's the Honorary Knight and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: I didn't know I'd see you two here. Well then... I won't stand on ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: I wanna offer some flowers to the Acting Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, Jean.

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: I guess you must be quite close to Master Jean? She's an incredibly upright and diligent woman, talented and always gets the job done. Honest, kind, gentle, not to mention...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, we get it! She's pretty great!

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: Sorry, once I get talking about Master Jean, I get a bit excited...

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: This time tomorrow, I'll finish composing my poem, pick a fresh dandelion bouquet, head over to the office, and hand the flowers to the guard.

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: It's just... the bouquet, and the poem... I don't know. Hmm... best not sign them after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Wait a second, it's only normal to sign them! Why does that bother you so much?

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: Knowing Master Jean's conscientious nature, I'm afraid she'll send a gift in return if she sees my name...

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: She's so busy, I wouldn't want my gift to create more work for her. If I can get this bouquet on her desk, that's enough for me.

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: But then... won't an untraceable bouquet create suspicion? Oh! What should I do?

choices.text: I agree, you should avoid signing it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Jean's definitely the kind of woman who'd come looking for you if she saw your name! If you really wanna spare her the effort, best leave it unsigned.

response.speaker: Ellin
response.text: Right! Glad you agree! It's not without its risks, but her extreme conscientiousness is what I like about her. So for me, raising a bit of suspicion is a risk worth taking...

response.speaker: Ellin
response.text: That's that taken care of, then. A thousand thanks for your advice, I'll remember it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're welcome, chin up!

response.speaker: Ellin
response.text: Will do!

choices.text: I think you should ponder the matter a while longer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No rush, mull it over!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In any case, it's totally up to you. Is it more important to you for her to remember the person who sent her the flowers, or for her to simply feel respected and loved?

response.speaker: Ellin
response.text: Huh... I never thought about it that way... Hmm... The important thing is... how I feel.

choices.text: I disagree, you should definitely sign your name.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: For sure! A random anonymous gift will definitely get thrown away!

response.speaker: Ellin
response.text: R—Really? You sound so sure! Well, I guess I better include my name...

talks.objective: Listen to and solve the troubles of the citizenry

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You there, are you looking for help from the bard? We're his assistants, why don't you tell us what's on your mind?

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: Oh! Uh... really? O—Okay then... here goes!

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: I—I'm just such a huge fan of Mondstadt's idol... Barbara-sama...! You must have heard of her? She's the super cute one at the Church of Favonius!

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: Not to mention gentle, and she always lifts the people of Mondstadt's spirits with her smile and songs. I'm such a big fan, I even got a few like-minded friends together, and well... what I mean to say is...

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: ...You guessed it! I'm the head of the Barbara Fan Club!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... pretty pleased about it too... by the sound of things...

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: I carry the hopes and expectations of every member of the fan club on my shoulders. At this special time of year, I've pledged to send our blessings to Barbara-sama herself!

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: Of course, as a level-headed adult, I would never wanna cause her any disturbance. I'm just waiting for my time slot with the bard, so I can explain the plan...

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: ...Take all the flowers picked by our members and turn them into a huge, giant flower statue! Then, to give her a huge surprise, place it outside the rear entrance of the Church.

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: As for the love poem, we don't need any help! We're planning to do it on our own and hang it on the statue itself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... this giant statue—

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: ...Will be about two stories high...!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That sounds like it might just cause her some disturbance.

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: But it's all in good faith, don't you see?! When Barbara-sama catches sight of it, she'll feel the burning flames of our everlasting love!

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: So, what do you think?

choices.text: You know what? Go for it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Something that size is bound to be... impressive. She'll love it!

response.speaker: Albert
response.text: Right?! I knew it was a great idea, haha.

response.speaker: Albert
response.text: Thanks for your suggestions, both of you. I gotta go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He sure left in a hurry!

choices.text: Give this one some more thought, perhaps.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A two-story gift? More like a gift out of a horror story!

response.speaker: Albert
response.text: Huh... You think so...?

response.speaker: Albert
response.text: But, how else will she know of our existence?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gee, how WILL she know...

response.speaker: Albert
response.text: Umm... well... now that you mention it, um...

choices.text: Are you serious? You need to put a stop to all this immediately!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A level-headed adult? Huh... more like a dunderheaded infant!

response.speaker: Albert
response.text: Huh? But — gifts have to make a lasting impression!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, it'll create a lasting impression alright! The Knights of Favonius will have you escorted away.

response.speaker: Albert
response.text: Really? B—But...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But nothing!

response.speaker: Albert
response.text: Okay, okay! *sigh* I've got it.

talks.objective: Listen to and solve the troubles of the citizenry

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tone-Deaf Bard! We dished out some advice, just like you said! How did we do?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hmm... Seems like my gestures weren't always translated into the advice I intended to give.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I guess I need to work on my communication for next time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh?! Next time?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: So, who else needs some help around here...
Hmm, what are you three up to? Mind if I get in on the action?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Kaeya! Are you also here for romantic guidance?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Haha, it's the greatest bard in town. And now, the greatest romantic advisor in town, no doubt.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Still, don't you have other business to attend to?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Oh! You mean, teaching people how to compose love poems?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Exactly that. I heard you were teaching classes in the plaza, so I came right away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Kaeya? You wanna learn how to compose love poems, too?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I thought Kaeya wouldn't need any help in that department.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: I'm not too shabby. Nevertheless, I'd like to register for the fast-track classes.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: How come? You're a smooth talker, do you really need my guidance?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: The real question is, are you willing to take me on as a student?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Of course! When the Mora comes knocking, who am I to keep the door closed?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Haha... Well then, I guess I'm enrolled.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: And as your student, may I make some reasonable demands?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aha, Paimon knew there was more to it!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Demands? *sigh* Let's hear them.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: As students, aside from attending class, we also need homework exercises.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Surely a well-designed course would require us to put our knowledge into practice, and then... have our teacher correct the poems we compose.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean, Venti has to correct the students' homework?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Precisely. All in exchange for payment, naturally. These are my demands.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Or to put it another way, I'm actually gonna have to work for a living!

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Hahaha, is that so bad? I just think that with things like this, you should see them all the way through.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: More fun for everyone involved, don't you think? What do you say?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I feel like Kaeya's knack for mischief is at play here...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Still, correcting homework... this is indeed a vital step.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: And I am curious to see the fruits of my students' labor... Hm. Congratulations, Kaeya, your demands have been accepted!

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: As I expected, a reasonable and down-to-earth teacher.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hoooold your horses, I have a demand for you, too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cool... a coercion contest...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A showdown between the pros.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I will pay special attention to your homework and guarantee that you will see improvement in your studies! But as for your tuition fee... some Windblume Festival-exclusive Applebloom Cider should do the trick.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hehe, what with you and Master Diluc being on such good terms and all, that shouldn't be a problem, should it?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Haha — steady now, let's not overestimate my abilities. Still, one bottle of the good stuff in exchange for your guidance... Not an opportunity to pass up.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Whoa, "one" bottle? Make that three!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Geez! Give him an inch and he'll take a mile!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Please? Please, please?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Deal.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Marvelous! Grab some paper and make your way over, Professor Venti's poetry masterclass is now in session!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's that paper the Tone-Deaf Bard pulled out of his pocket...? And whose names are those?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Albert... Ellin... Marvin... Timaeus... Kaeya... Bennett.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Oh, uh — present!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Bennett's really fired up for this...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: So you're Bennett? Excellent, I like your enthusiasm. Make sure to channel that vigor into your poetry.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Yes, Sir!

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Even adventurers want to learn how to write poetry... I see this is going to be a popular class.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tone-Deaf Bard's gonna make a fortune...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: My dear students... In a moment, we will gather by the terrace in front of the Cathedral, where I will divulge to you my experiences and techniques in the art of poetic composition.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: After class, I would like every one of you to compose a love poem and hand it to me for... uh... constructive criticism.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: As for your tuition fees, by all means, wait until the course is over before paying. But don't even think about vanishing...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: ...In addition to Mora, payment in alcohol is also warmly welcomed!

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: A quick question, Sir... Does our special arrangement still stand?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: But of course! And when the time comes, you can hand in your homework first!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Traveler, I'd like you and I to collect the homework submissions together.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Does that fall under the assistant's duties? Do we get paid for this?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Think of it as an initiation into Mondstadt's traditional culture — an opportunity to immerse yourselves in the Windblume Festival! I'm going to great lengths here to make sure you're a part of the festivities.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Not to mention, it would entitle you to a share of the remuneration...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! Sir, yes Sir!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Good! In that case, when Kaeya's finished with his homework, let's go and look for him at the Knights of Favonius Headquarters.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: But for now, I've got classes to teach! Traveler, why not make the most of it and check things out in the meantime?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: The vendors in Mondstadt have arranged all sorts of festive activities. Don't forget to try them out!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: You did a great job, hehe! Thank you!
